newsitem.title: USA: Astoria to acquire Greater New York for $293 million.
newsitem.headline: Astoria to acquire Greater New York for $293 million.

text.p: Astoria Financial Corp. said Monday it will acquire Greater New York Savings Bank for $293 million in stock and cash, creating the third-largest publicly traded thrift in New York and the 13th biggest in the nation.
The transaction, which gives Astoria a presence in Brooklyn, the most populous of New York City's five boroughs, will form a regional savings and loan powerhouse with $9.8 billion in assets.
The combined company will operate 59 banking offices in the New York metropolitan area.

"The strategic in-market acquisition of The Greater's banking franchise represents an important complementary fit for us, further strengthening our current banking franchise," Astoria President George L. Engelke Jr. said in a statement.
Gerard Keegan, chairman, president and chief executive of Greater New York, will join Astoria as a director and vice chairman and chief administrative officer.

Under terms of the definitive agreement, holders of Greater New York common stock will receive either 0.50 share of Astoria Financial common stock or $19 in cash for each share, subject to 75 percent of Greater New York holders receiving Astoria stock and 25 percent receiving cash.
Greater New York's stock slipped 50 cents to $17.375 on the Nasdaq market while Astoria Financial lost $1.875 to $36, also on Nasdaq.
The transaction, which is expected to close by the end of September, will immediately add to Astoria's earnings per share, the statement said.
Astoria said it estimated that operating efficiencies as a result of the transaction will produce cost savings equal to 45 percent of Greater New York's non-interest expenses.
The companies said the transaction will be accounted for as a purchase and will not affect Astoria's ability to repurchase shares under its current stock repurchase programme.
The agreement includes a termination fee payable to Astoria if the transaction is not completed under certain circumstances.
In addition, Greater New York granted Astoria an option to purchase shares equal to 19.9 percent of Greater New York's currently outstanding common stock under certain conditions.
The transaction, still subject to approval of the shareholders of both companies, was unanimouosly approved by the boards of both companies.

They also said the outstanding shares of the 12 percent noncumulative Preferred Stock, Series B, of Greater New York will be converted into a newly created series of preferred stock of Astoria Financial Corp. with substantially identical, and no less favourable terms.
